text: The diffraction pattern of a light of wavelength $400\mathrm{nm}$ diffracting from a slit of width $0.2\mathrm{mm}$ is focused on the focal plane of a convex lens of focal length $100\mathrm{cm}$. The width of the $1^{\text{st}}$ secondary maxima will be :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 30th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For single-slit diffraction focused by a lens of focal length $f$, the minima on the focal plane lie at

$y_{m}=\frac{mλf}{a},m=1,2,3,\ldots$

The first secondary maximum lies between the first and second minima, so its width is

$y_{2}-y_{1}=\frac{λf}{a}$

With $λ=400\times 10^{-9}\text{m}$, $a=0.2\times 10^{-3}\text{m}$ and $f=1\text{m}$:

$\frac{λf}{a}=\frac{400\times 10^{-9}\times 1}{0.2\times 10^{-3}}=2\times 10^{-3}\text{m}=2\text{mm}$

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 30th January Morning Shift

text:
Two thermodynamical processes are shown in the figure. The molar heat capacity for process A and B are $\mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{A}}$ and $\mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{B}}$. The molar heat capacity at constant pressure and constant volume are represented by $\mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{P}}$ and $\mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{V}}$, respectively. Choose the correct statement.


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 30th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For process $\mathrm{A}$

$\begin{array}{l} \log P=γ\log \mathrm{V}\Rightarrow \mathrm{P}=\mathrm{V}^{γ},(γ>1) \\ PV^{-γ}=\text{Constant} \end{array}$

$C_{A}=C_{V}+\frac{R}{1+γ}$ ..... (i)

Likewise for process $\mathrm{B}\to PV^{-1}=$ Constant

$\begin{array}{l} C_{B}=C_{v}+\dfrac{R}{1+1} \\ C_{B}=C_{v}+\dfrac{R}{2}\text{..... (ii)} \\ C_{P}=C_{v}+R\text{..... (iii)} \end{array}$

By (i), (ii) & (iii)

$C_{P}>C_{B}>C_{A}>C_{v}$, which is option (A).

Note: in the original paper no option matched this result, so this option has been written in to give the question a correct answer.

text:
All surfaces shown in figure are assumed to be frictionless and the pulleys and the string are light. The acceleration of the block of mass $2\mathrm{kg}$ is :


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 30th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]

The 4 kg block hangs from a movable pulley. When it descends by $x$, the string on both sides of the movable pulley lengthens by $x$, so the 2 kg block moves up the incline by $2x$. With the 4 kg block accelerating downward at $a$, the 2 kg block accelerates up the incline at $2a$, and the tension $T$ is the same throughout the light string.

For the 4 kg block, two strands pull the movable pulley up:

$40-2T=4a$

For the 2 kg block along the incline, the component of weight is $2\times 10\times \sin 30^{\circ }=10\text{N}$:

$T-10=2(2a)=4a$

Doubling the second equation and adding it to the first:

$20=12a\Rightarrow a=\dfrac{5}{3}\text{m s}^{-2}$

The acceleration of the 2 kg block is $2a=\dfrac{10}{3}\text{m s}^{-2}=\dfrac{g}{3}$.

Hence, the correct option is (D).

text: An electric toaster has resistance of $60\Omega$ at room temperature $(27^{\circ }\mathrm{C})$. The toaster is connected to a $220\mathrm{V}$ supply. If the current flowing through it reaches $2.75\mathrm{A}$, the temperature attained by toaster is around : ( if $α=2\times 10^{-4}$/${}^{\circ }\mathrm{C}$)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 30th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
At room temperature $27^{\circ }\text{C}$, $R_{27}=60\Omega$. When $2.75\text{A}$ flows on the $220\text{V}$ supply, the hot resistance is

$R_{T}=\dfrac{220}{2.75}=80\Omega$

Using $R_{T}=R_{27}[1+α(T-27)]$:

$\dfrac{80}{60}=1+2\times 10^{-4}(T-27)\Rightarrow 2\times 10^{-4}(T-27)=\dfrac{1}{3}$

$T-27=\dfrac{1}{6\times 10^{-4}}\approx 1667^{\circ }\text{C}$

This is the rise in temperature, so the temperature attained is

$T\approx 1667+27=1694^{\circ }\text{C}$

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 30th January Morning Shift

text: A spherical body of mass $100\mathrm{g}$ is dropped from a height of $10\mathrm{m}$ from the ground. After hitting the ground, the body rebounds to a height of $5\mathrm{m}$. The impulse of force imparted by the ground to the body is given by : (given, $\mathrm{g}=9.8\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 30th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Mass $m=0.1$ kg. Speed just before hitting the ground, after falling 10 m:

$v_{1}=\sqrt{2gh_{1}}=\sqrt{2\times 9.8\times 10}=\sqrt{196}=14\text{m s}^{-1}\text{(downward)}$

Speed just after leaving the ground, to rise 5 m:

$v_{2}=\sqrt{2gh_{2}}=\sqrt{2\times 9.8\times 5}=\sqrt{98}=7\sqrt{2}\approx 9.9\text{m s}^{-1}\text{(upward)}$

Taking upward as positive, the impulse imparted by the ground equals the change in momentum:

$J=mv_{2}-m(-v_{1})=0.1(9.9+14)\approx 2.39\text{kg m s}^{-1}$

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 30th January Morning Shift

text:
Two cells are connected in opposition as shown. Cell $\mathrm{E}_{1}$ is of $8\mathrm{V}$ emf and $2\Omega$ internal resistance; the cell $\mathrm{E}_{2}$ is of $2\mathrm{V}$ emf and $4\Omega$ internal resistance. The terminal potential difference of cell $\mathrm{E}_{2}$ is $__________ V$.


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 30th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In the figure the negative terminals of both cells are joined at B, so the two emfs oppose each other in the single loop. The net emf drives the current through the total internal resistance:

$I=\dfrac{E_{1}-E_{2}}{r_{1}+r_{2}}=\dfrac{8-2}{2+4}=1\text{A}$

The larger emf $E_{1}$ sets the direction of this current, so inside $E_{2}$ the current enters at the positive terminal (C side) and leaves at the negative terminal (B side): $E_{2}$ is being charged.


[IMG]

For a cell being charged, the terminal potential difference is its emf plus the drop across its internal resistance:

$V_{C}-V_{B}=E_{2}+Ir_{2}=2+1\times 4=6\text{V}$

Hence, the answer is 6.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 30th January Morning Shift

text: The displacement and the increase in the velocity of a moving particle in the time interval of $t$ to $(t+1)\mathrm{s}$ are $125\mathrm{m}$ and $50\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$, respectively. The distance travelled by the particle in $(\mathrm{t}+2)^{\mathrm{th}}\mathrm{s}$ is $_________ m$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 30th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let the acceleration of the particle be $a$, which is assumed to be uniform.

The increase in velocity in a time interval of $\Delta t=(t+1)-t=1\text{s}$ is given as $50\text{m/s}$. 

Using the relation for acceleration:

$a=\frac{\Delta v}{\Delta t}$

$a=\frac{50}{1}=50\text{m/s}^{2}$

Let the velocity of the particle at time $t$ be $v_{t}$. 

The displacement in the time interval from $t$ to $(t+1)\text{s}$ is given by:

$s=v_{t}\Delta t+\frac{1}{2}a(\Delta t)^{2}$

Substitute the given values into the equation:

$125=v_{t}(1)+\frac{1}{2}(50)(1)^{2}$

$125=v_{t}+25$

$v_{t}=100\text{m/s}$

Now, the velocity at the end of this interval, which is at time $(t+1)\text{s}$, becomes:

$v_{t+1}=v_{t}+a(1)$

$v_{t+1}=100+50=150\text{m/s}$

The $(t+2)^{\text{th}}\text{s}$ represents the time interval from time $(t+1)\text{s}$ to $(t+2)\text{s}$, which is also an interval of $1\text{s}$.

Since the particle moves in a straight line with a positive velocity and positive acceleration, the distance travelled is equal to the magnitude of the displacement in this interval.

The distance travelled in the $(t+2)^{\text{th}}\text{s}$ is:

$s_{(t+2)}=v_{t+1}(1)+\frac{1}{2}a(1)^{2}$

$s_{(t+2)}=150(1)+\frac{1}{2}(50)(1)^{2}$

$s_{(t+2)}=150+25=175\text{m}$

The distance travelled by the particle in $(t+2)^{\text{th}}\text{s}$ is $175\text{m}$.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 30th January Morning Shift

text:
Each of three blocks $\mathrm{P},\mathrm{Q}$ and $\mathrm{R}$ shown in figure has a mass of $3\mathrm{kg}$. Each of the wires $\mathrm{A}$ and $\mathrm{B}$ has cross-sectional area $0.005\mathrm{cm}^{2}$ and Young's modulus $2\times 10^{11}\mathrm{N}\mathrm{m}^{-2}$. Neglecting friction, the longitudinal strain on wire $B$ is $________$ $\times 10^{-4}$. (Take $\mathrm{g}=10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$)


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 30th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Wire A joins P to Q, and wire B joins Q to R over the pulley. With no friction, only the weight of R accelerates the three $3\text{kg}$ blocks together:

$a=\dfrac{m_{R}g}{m_{P}+m_{Q}+m_{R}}=\dfrac{3\times 10}{9}=\dfrac{10}{3}\text{m s}^{-2}$

Wire B pulls both P and Q (through wire A), so its tension is

$T_{B}=(m_{P}+m_{Q})a=6\times \dfrac{10}{3}=20\text{N}$

With area $A=0.005\text{cm}^{2}=5\times 10^{-7}\text{m}^{2}$:

$\text{stress}=\dfrac{T_{B}}{A}=\dfrac{20}{5\times 10^{-7}}=4\times 10^{7}\text{N m}^{-2}$

$\text{strain}=\dfrac{\text{stress}}{Y}=\dfrac{4\times 10^{7}}{2\times 10^{11}}=2\times 10^{-4}$

Hence, the answer is 2.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 30th January Morning Shift
